text: The direct product of groups G and H has componentwise multiplication: (g,h)(g',h')=(gg',hh'). Its identity is (e_G,e_H).

text: The symmetry group of a regular n-gon, n>=3, is generated by rotation r and reflection s: r^n=s^2=1 and srs=r^(-1); its order is 2n.
provenance: Original formulation and examples of standard mathematics; independently checked from the displayed definition or calculation. Reference context: J. S. Milne, Group Theory, https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/GT.pdf. No source prose reproduced.

text: The quaternion group Q_8 is {+/-1,+/-i,+/-j,+/-k}, with i^2=j^2=k^2=ijk=-1. It has eight elements and is nonabelian.
provenance: Original formulation and examples of standard mathematics; independently checked from the displayed definition or calculation. Reference context: J. S. Milne, Group Theory, https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/GT.pdf. No source prose reproduced.

text: The symmetric group S_n consists of all bijections of {1,...,n}, with composition. Its order is n!, and composition applies the right factor first.
provenance: Original formulation and examples of standard mathematics; independently checked from the displayed definition or calculation. Reference context: J. S. Milne, Group Theory, https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/GT.pdf. No source prose reproduced.

text: The polynomial ring R[x] consists of finite formal sums of powers of x with coefficients in a commutative ring R. Addition combines like powers; multiplication distributes and adds exponents.
provenance: Original formulation and examples of standard mathematics; independently checked from the displayed definition or calculation. Reference context: Stacks Project, commutative algebra conventions, https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00AQ. No source prose reproduced.

text: The dual-number ring over the real numbers is R[epsilon]/(epsilon^2). Its product is (a+b*epsilon)(c+d*epsilon)=ac+(ad+bc)*epsilon.
provenance: Original formulation and examples of standard mathematics; independently checked from the displayed definition or calculation. Reference context: Stacks Project, commutative algebra conventions, https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00AQ. No source prose reproduced.

text: The localization of the integers at all nonzero integers is the rational field Q, with a/b represented by an integer numerator and nonzero denominator.
provenance: Original formulation and examples of standard mathematics; independently checked from the displayed definition or calculation. Reference context: Stacks Project, localization, https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00CM. No source prose reproduced.

text: For modules M and N over a commutative ring R, M tensor_R N is the free R-module on pairs (m,n) modulo additivity in both slots and relations (r*m,n)=(m,r*n)=r*(m,n).
provenance: Original formulation and examples of standard mathematics; independently checked from the displayed definition or calculation. Reference context: Stacks Project, tensor products, https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00CV. No source prose reproduced.

text: The discrete metric on a set X is d(x,y)=0 for equal points and 1 otherwise.
provenance: Original formulation and examples of standard mathematics; independently checked from the displayed definition or calculation. Reference context: Jiri Lebl, Basic Analysis, metric spaces, https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_metric.html. No source prose reproduced.

text: The taxicab metric on R^2 is d((x,y),(u,v))=|x-u|+|y-v|. Triangle inequalities in each coordinate establish the metric axioms.
provenance: Original formulation and examples of standard mathematics; independently checked from the displayed definition or calculation. Reference context: Jiri Lebl, Basic Analysis, metric spaces, https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_metric.html. No source prose reproduced.

text: The Cantor set is the intersection of the closed sets left after successive removal of each interval's open middle third, starting with [0,1]. It is compact.
provenance: Original formulation and examples of standard mathematics; independently checked from the displayed definition or calculation. Reference context: Jiri Lebl, Basic Analysis, completeness and compactness, https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_metcompact.html. No source prose reproduced.

text: The completion of Q with its usual metric is R. Its points are equivalence classes of rational Cauchy sequences; equivalent sequences have difference tending to zero.
provenance: Original formulation and examples of standard mathematics; independently checked from the displayed definition or calculation. Reference context: Jiri Lebl, Basic Analysis, completeness and compactness, https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_metcompact.html. No source prose reproduced.

text: For a unit vector u in R^n, the map P(v)=(u dot v)u is an orthogonal projection. It satisfies P^2=P, with image span(u) and kernel u-perpendicular.
provenance: Original formulation and examples of standard mathematics; independently checked from the displayed definition or calculation. Reference context: Gilbert Strang, MIT 18.06 Linear Algebra, https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/18-06-linear-algebra-spring-2010/. No source prose reproduced.

text: The n-by-n matrix with ones on the superdiagonal and zeros elsewhere shifts coordinates. Its nth power is zero, but its (n-1)st power is nonzero.
provenance: Original formulation and examples of standard mathematics; independently checked from the displayed definition or calculation. Reference context: Gilbert Strang, MIT 18.06 Linear Algebra, https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/18-06-linear-algebra-spring-2010/. No source prose reproduced.

text: For x^2+a*x+b, the matrix [[0,-b],[1,-a]] has characteristic polynomial x^2+a*x+b.
provenance: Original formulation and examples of standard mathematics; independently checked from the displayed definition or calculation. Reference context: Gilbert Strang, MIT 18.06 Linear Algebra, https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/18-06-linear-algebra-spring-2010/. No source prose reproduced.

text: The kernel of a linear map T:V->W is ker(T)={v:T(v)=0}. Linearity makes this set a vector subspace.
provenance: Original formulation and examples of standard mathematics; independently checked from the displayed definition or calculation. Reference context: Jiri Lebl, Basic Analysis, vector spaces and convexity, https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_vectorspaces.html. No source prose reproduced.

text: For |r|<1, the geometric series sum(r^n), n=0 to infinity, converges to 1/(1-r). Its partial sum through n=N is (1-r^(N+1))/(1-r).
provenance: Original formulation and examples of standard mathematics; independently checked from the displayed definition or calculation. Reference context: Jiri Lebl, Basic Analysis I, https://jirka.org/ra/realanal.pdf. No source prose reproduced.

text: The function f(x)=exp(-1/x^2) for x!=0, with f(0)=0, is smooth. Every derivative at zero vanishes, although f is positive away from zero.
provenance: Original formulation and examples of standard mathematics; independently checked from the displayed definition or calculation. Reference context: Jiri Lebl, Basic Analysis I, https://jirka.org/ra/realanal.pdf. No source prose reproduced.

text: The convex hull of a subset A of a real vector space consists of all finite sums sum(t_i*a_i), with a_i in A, t_i>=0, and sum(t_i)=1.
provenance: Original formulation and examples of standard mathematics; independently checked from the displayed definition or calculation. Reference context: Jiri Lebl, Basic Analysis, vector spaces and convexity, https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_vectorspaces.html. No source prose reproduced.

text: On [-1,1], the functions f_n(x)=sqrt(x^2+1/n) approximate |x| uniformly because 0<=f_n(x)-|x|<=1/sqrt(n).
provenance: Original formulation and examples of standard mathematics; independently checked from the displayed definition or calculation. Reference context: Jiri Lebl, Basic Analysis, pointwise and uniform convergence, https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_puconv.html. No source prose reproduced.
